extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline, and parties involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order documenting a proposed settlement between the OED Director and a registered patent attorney, setting out stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions under USPTO disciplinary rules. Used to determine and record discipline, publication, and notice obligations arising from attorney misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. §11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed settlement agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint. The proposed settlement agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. §11.26, resolves all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement must include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and must satisfy 37 C.F.R. §11.26 to be approved by the Under Secretary/USPTO Director or his designate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules to registered practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant hereto, Respondent has been registered as an attorney to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. §10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners before the USPTO are bound by 37 C.F.R. §10.20 et seq.; disciplinary proceedings may rely on registration status (including registration number) and state licensure information.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law ethical violations as grounds for USPTO discipline (reciprocal discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner disciplined on ethical grounds by a state (here, public censure by the Supreme Court of New Hampshire) can be the basis for USPTO discipline. Respondent acknowledges his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. §§10.23(a) and 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5) by being disciplined on ethical grounds by the State of New Hampshire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative action by a state bar (e.g., public censure for violation of state Rules of Professional Conduct) can be treated as grounds for USPTO disciplinary action; the Final Order cites the specific USPTO regulations used to convert state discipline into USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline: dishonesty and misrepresentation (state RPC 8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's preparation and submission of a false report to a faculty committee and false statements about attending classes involved dishonesty and/or misrepresentation in violation of New Hampshire Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(c) and 8.4(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misconduct involving fabrication, false statements to committees or third parties, and other dishonesty is a basis for professional discipline; the Final Order explains the underlying factual misconduct (fabricated report, false claims of attendance) as the factual predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof for establishing misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear and convincing evidence reflected that Respondent engaged in misconduct; therefore, clear and convincing evidence established a violation of New Hampshire Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary findings rest on a 'clear and convincing' evidentiary standard as applied to the facts establishing misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available/ordered sanctions (public reprimand and related measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: As agreed and ordered: (a) Respondent is publicly reprimanded; (b) the OED Director shall publish the Final Order; (c) the OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette (Notice of Reprimand) describing the respondent, registration number, violations, and the basis for discipline; (d) the OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public; and (e) the OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions include public reprimand and publication; the Notice must identify the practitioner, cite the violated rules and statutes, summarize the misconduct, and cite statutory/regulatory authority (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.26 and 11.59). Notice and publication obligations extend to state agencies, courts, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for Official Gazette notice of reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Reprimand published in the Official Gazette must identify the respondent by name and registration number, state that the respondent has been reprimanded by the USPTO for violating specified regulations (here, 37 C.F.R. §§10.23(a) and 10.23(b)(6) via 10.23(c)(5)), and describe the factual basis (public censure by the state for violations of state RPCs in connection with specified misconduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order provides an example Notice of Reprimand text that includes name, registration number, rule citations, factual summary of misconduct, and statutory authority; publication should follow that model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §§11.26 and 11.59; respondents may be disciplined under these statutes and regulations for professional misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders should cite the controlling statutory and regulatory provisions authorizing discipline, settlement approval, publication, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may specify cost allocation; here, the parties agreed to bear their own costs rather than imposing costs or fines on the respondent.
